analytic_fx.reading: gap(16) on the frozen grids: F 0.410 [0.380,0.447], X 0.385 [0.354,0.418] -- both far above the 0.20 gate. Difficulty is measured-matched: entropy 2.625 vs 2.693 nat, uniform-baseline KL 0.841 vs 0.773 (ratio 1.088). The analytic cost of forcing a two-group belief state is 0.000 nat in F (exact) and 0.063 nat in X, so the entire capacity-style asymmetry is 0.063 nat: any interaction must come from learnability, not representational capacity.

control_pilot_1600.model: dense GRU H=64, input 6, head 32; Adam 3e-3; batch 128
control_pilot_1600.reading: A dense 64-unit GRU control removes 80-90% of the uniform-baseline error on the theta-posterior target (KL 0.070-0.157 at 1600 updates against baselines 0.757-0.837), so the target is largely learnable in a 64-dimensional state. The residual is above the 0.05 nat headroom scale but the curves are still descending, so this pilot cannot distinguish genuine headroom from undertraining: the registered budget-doubling gate must decide. Note also that the analytic ceiling on the F-X capacity asymmetry is only 0.063 nat, i.e. the same order as the residual, leaving little room for an interaction.
control_pilot_1600.status: engineering pilot; not a verdict; superseded for the gate question by the budget-doubling run

gate_reading.compressibility: target not fully compressible into H=64 at this budget

control_pilot_budget_doubling.model: dense GRU H=64, input 6, head 32; Adam 3e-3; batch 128
control_pilot_budget_doubling.reading: Budget doubling decides the R2 compressibility question. From 1600 to 6400 updates the control's KL is flat (F seeds 0.070->0.080 and 0.157->0.137; X 0.081->0.081 and 0.076->0.077; all |delta| <= 0.010), so the residual is a genuine plateau, not undertraining. Residuals 0.077-0.137 nats sit above the 0.05 nat headroom scale => the theta posterior is NOT fully compressible into a 64-dimensional state and terminal headroom exists. Caveat: the analytic cost of forcing a two-group belief state is only 0.063 nat, and the dense control's X residual (0.081/0.077) is at or above that floor, so the headroom is not purely organisation-shaped -- a better model of any kind could capture part of it, and the interaction must be read as a learnability effect.
